 bl laca/k esa IV (2009) CPJ 19 (SC) NEW INDIA
 ASSURANCE CO. LTD. Vs. ZUARI INDUSTRIES LTD. &
 ORS. esa ekuuh; loksZPp U;k;ky; us fuEu fu/kkZfjr fd;k
 gS %& (i ) Insurance -Fire Incident--Proximate cause of damage
 flashover caused by short circuit -claim repudiated on ground
 that there was not 'sustained fire' -Word used in policy 'fire' not
5
'sustained fire' -court cannot add words to statute/document--
Fire efficient and active cause of damage proved--Insurer held
liable under policy
(ii) Insurance -Proximate cause of damage--
Contention, loss not caused by fire, but by stoppage of
electricity due to short circuit -Proximate cause of damage,
thermal shock, not fire--Claim repudiated -Proximate cause
not a cause nearest in time/place, but active and efficient cause
that sets in motion a train or chain of events which brings about
ultimate result without intervention of any other force working
from independent source--Fire was efficient and active cause
of damage proved -Insurer held liable under policy.

Act, 1986--Section 2(1) (g), 14 (1)(d), 23 -Insurance--
Accident of vehicle -Surveyor appointed -Overloading
alleged--Claim repudiated--Deficiency in service--District
Forum allowed complaint -State Commission allowed
appeal--National Commission dismissed revision -Hence
appeal Accident as caused on account of rash and negligent
driving of offending vehicle--FIR under
Section 337
,

,

of IPC registered against driver of vehicle--
Insurance Company not produced any evidence on record to
prove that accident occurred on account of overloading of
passengers in goods carrying vehicle--For the insurer to avoid
liability, breach of policy must be so fundamental in nature that
it brings contract to an end--Violation of policy conditions not
established--Repudiation not justified -Cost @Rs. 25,000/-
imposed.

LTD. Vs. NEW INDIA ASSURANCE CO. LTD. & ORS.
(i)
Insurance -Fire accident Insurance policy does not exclude
damage from fire due to poor maintenance, use of substandard
quality spares or inherent design defect in machine insured by
6
Insurance Company -While interpreting policy of insurance,
 Courts have to give natural meaning to expressions used in
 documents and it is not open to Court to make any addition to
 or subtraction from terms and conditions contained in Insurance
 Policy.
(ii)
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
--
Section 2(1) (g)
,
14 (1)(d)
,
21 (a) (i)
Insurance -Fire accident -Surveyor
 appointed -Loss assessed--Claim repudiated -Deficiency in
 service Insurance policy obtained by complainant company did
 not exclude liability of company in case fire took place due to
 poor maintenance, sub-standard quality of spares or
 manufacturing or inherent design defect in machine--Insurance
 policy cannot be said to be a service availed for commercial
 purpose within meaning of
section 2 (1) (d)
, of CP Act -
 Damage was not covered under warranty clause Repudiation
 not justified -Insurance Company is directed to pay amount of
 Rs. 78,25,005 to complainant -Litigation cost @ Rs. 25,000
 awarded.
